content_sections.body_text: Use was/were + verb-ing for an action in progress around a past time: ‘At four, I was reading the timetable.’ Timeline: action starts — 4:00 — action continues. Contrast the completed event: ‘The bus left at 4:15.’
content_sections.title: Show an ongoing past scene

content_sections.body_text: Source notice: ‘Bus 12 leaves at 4:15 from Gate 3.’ Recipient: a friend who cannot see it. Relay only the useful facts: ‘Bus 12 leaves at 4:15 from Gate 3.’ Check the bus, time, and gate against the notice; all three must match.
content_sections.title: Mediate a timetable detail

content_sections.body_text: With a friend: ‘Please help me read this.’ With unfamiliar station staff: ‘Excuse me. Could you help me read this timetable, please?’ Excuse me gets attention politely; could you help makes the request less direct; final please adds courtesy. The staff reply should provide an actual timetable detail.
content_sections.title: Explain the polite request

content_sections.body_text: In in-for-MA-tion /ˌɪn.fəˈmeɪ.ʃən/, /meɪ/ has the main word stress. Keep that vowel full, make the syllable a little longer and stronger, and allow a pitch change; say the other syllables more lightly. Then explain what you were doing, request help, and relay the bus, time, and gate exactly.
content_sections.title: Stress a syllable and integrate
